  POST HEARING REPLY BRIEF, PROPOSED FINDINGS OF FACT, CONCLUSIONS
                 OF LAW AND ORDERING PROVISIONS​
                 OF INTERVENOR GRETCHEN NOELKE

COMES NOW, Gretchen Noelke, pro se, to submit his Post Hearing Reply Brief with Proposed Findings
of Fact, Conclusions of Law and Ordering Provisions, pursuant to SOAH Order Nos. 6 and 32 in this
case.

I.​     Introduction
      A.​ Intervenor Gretchen Noelke submits this Reply Brief to address the fundamental evidentiary and
          legal deficiencies in the Applicant’s case.
      B.​ She has previously timely filed her initial post hearing brief . See Item 6200. Applicants did not
          respond, directly or indirectly, to that brief.
      C.​ She specifically opposes Routes 487, 494 and 499, all of which include Link M7; and, ​
          Routes 547, 548, 295, 296 and 297, all of which include Link M22.

11. Legal argument

      A.​ Gretchen Noelke argues that the Applicants’ failure to consider her Noelke Wilhelm Ranch as a
          legacy ranch recognized by the Family Land Heritage Program through the Texas Department of
          Agriculture is a failure to properly consider and weigh the PURA factors of community, aesthetic
         and historical values. See PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(A) and (C).
    B.​ She further argues that Applicants’ failure to address the flooding of Calf Creek on her Noelke
         Wilhelm Ranch is a failure to properly consider and weigh the PURA factors of environmental
         integrity and aesthetic values. See PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(C) and (D).
    C.​ Applicants’ failed to rebut, directly or indirectly, the factual and legal basis supporting A and B
         above. Applicants admitted no evidence, and thereby there is nothing in the administrative record,
         contradicting her allegations.
    D.​ She aligns herself with the legal arguments made by Wade Noelke of NF5, as Applicants’
         proposed line intersects family land passed down through the same ancestor. See NF5 Post
         Hearing Brief, Item 6316.
    E.​ Finally, she aligns herself with American Stewards of Liberty and the other Intervenors arguing
         that Applicants have failed to establish a need for this project. See ASL’s Initial Closing
         Argument, Item 6225.

III. Conclusion​
Gretchen Noelke requests FOF, COL and ordering provisions that reflect that Applicants have not proven
that they qualify for the CCN. First, they haven’t established the proper need for the project. Second, they
have not by a preponderance of the evidence established that they considered and weighed the
environmental integrity and the community, aesthetic and historical values related to her Noelke Wilhelm
Ranch.

She recommends the following Conclusion of Law: The CCN amendments are not approved by this
Order since it will adversely affect community values, historical and aesthetic values, and environmental
integrity of certain properties. PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(A), (C) and (D).

WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, Intervenor Gretchen Noelke respectfully prays that the
Administrative Law Judges recommend to the PUC to refuse to issue the CCN in 59475 and that they
fairly consider the FOF, COL and ordering provisions above requested by her.

Signed June 26, 2026

Respectfully submitted,​
